findings.finding: createAttachment accepts calls without checking for an active execution, sends native write IPC and resolves the canonical filename.
Parent always writes the artifact. It adds a pending preview/model attachment only when agentToolCallIds has a current tool for that agent and Karton is available.
Current tool ID is set before script execution and cleared in finally after clearPendingOutputs. Idle callbacks after that point do not populate a future-tool queue.
Worker create-attachment-result appends to per-agent collection only if one exists, then resolves filename in all successful cases. Collection is reset per execution and deleted on completion.
drainPendingAttachments drains already-associated tool attachment previews after a step; it is not a general persistent idle-attachment queue.

conclusion: Preserve successful idle writes and filename return without silently attaching them to an unrelated future model step. When an event callback creates an attachment while a tool for the same agent/context is active, associate it with that active tool, as upstream does. Native UI may report idle-created artifacts separately. Do not retain forever an empty-tool-ID attachment/error bucket.
status: Implemented and verified: SandboxHost attributes event-origin writes only to the current same-agent/context tool, while true idle writes keep empty tool identity and successful filename return. Root AgentToolHost owns ignoring empty-ID metadata buckets.
